title: Cybersecurity's Strategic Inflection Point
gist: A WEF Global Future Council report argues cybersecurity is still treated as a technical cost although it is a condition of economic resilience, and sets a 2027 leadership agenda: shared vocabulary, business-value framing, comparable resilience measures and sustainable financing for under-resourced environments.

insights.claim: Cybersecurity has become a condition of economic resilience, but governance, investment and measurement practices have not kept pace and most institutions treat it as a technical cost.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Gap between cyber risk and spend implies underinvestment.

insights.claim: The report's four areas are a shared vocabulary for decision-makers, reframing cyber as business value, measures that let resilience be compared across institutions and economies, and sustainable financing for under-resourced environments.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Agenda items likely to shape cyber disclosure and insurance metrics.
insights.locator: The report sets out key areas
